def max_distance_after_one_swap(n, a):
    min_index = a.index(1)
    max_index = a.index(n)
    
    # Calculate initial distance
    initial_distance = abs(min_index - max_index)
    
    # Try swapping the minimum element with its adjacent elements
    swap_with_left = abs((min_index - 1) - max_index) if min_index > 0 else float('-inf')
    swap_with_right = abs((min_index + 1) - max_index) if min_index < n - 1 else float('-inf')
    
    # Try swapping the maximum element with its adjacent elements
    swap_with_left_max = abs((max_index - 1) - min_index) if max_index > 0 else float('-inf')
    swap_with_right_max = abs((max_index + 1) - min_index) if max_index < n - 1 else float('-inf')
    
    # Return the maximum possible distance after one swap
    return max(initial_distance, swap_with_left, swap_with_right, swap_with_left_max, swap_with_right_max)

def max_distance(n, a):
    min_index = a.index(1)
    max_index = a.index(n)
    
    # Calculate initial distance
    initial_distance = abs(min_index - max_index)
    
    # Try swapping the minimum element with every other element except itself
    best_distance = initial_distance
    for i in range(n):
        if a[i] != 1 and a[i] != n:
            temp = a[min_index]
            a[min_index] = a[i]
            a[i] = temp
            
            new_min_index = a.index(1)
            new_max_index = a.index(n)
            new_distance = abs(new_min_index - new_max_index)
            
            if new_distance > best_distance:
                best_distance = new_distance
            
            # Swap back to original state
            temp = a[min_index]
            a[min_index] = a[i]
            a[i] = temp
    
    return best_distance

    min_index = a.index(1)
    max_index = a.index(n)
    
    # Calculate initial distance
    initial_distance = abs(min_index - max_index)
    
    # Calculate distances after potential swaps
    possible_distances = [
        abs((min_index + 1) - max_index),
        abs(min_index - (max_index + 1)),
        abs((min_index - 1) - max_index),
        abs(min_index - (max_index - 1))
    ]
    
    # Return the maximum possible distance
    return max(max(initial_distance, max(possible_distances)), initial_distance)

    min_index = arr.index(1)
    max_index = arr.index(n)
    
    # Calculate initial distance
    initial_distance = abs(min_index - max_index)
    
    # Try swapping the minimum with every other element
    min_swaps = [abs(arr[i] - n) + abs(i - min_index) for i in range(n) if arr[i] != 1]
    
    # Try swapping the maximum with every other element
    max_swaps = [abs(arr[i] - 1) + abs(i - max_index) for i in range(n) if arr[i] != n]
    
    # Combine both lists and find the maximum possible distance
    all_swaps = min_swaps + max_swaps
    result = max(all_swaps + [initial_distance])
    
    return result

    max_index = a.index(n)
    
    # Calculate the current distance
    current_distance = abs(min_index - max_index)

    # Return the maximum distance achieved by either current or new distances
    return max(current_distance, max_new_distance)

def max_distance_after_one_swap(n, arr):
    min_index = arr.index(1)
    max_index = arr.index(n)
    
    # Calculate initial distance
    initial_distance = abs(min_index - max_index)
    
    # Try swapping the min and max with their neighbors
    potential_distances = [
        abs((min_index + 1 if min_index != n-1 else min_index) - max_index),
        abs((max_index + 1 if max_index != n-1 else max_index) - min_index),
        abs((min_index - 1 if min_index != 0 else min_index) - max_index),
        abs((max_index - 1 if max_index != 0 else max_index) - min_index)
    ]
    
    # Return the maximum of initial distance and potential distances
    return max(initial_distance, *potential_distances)
